statusText: Mapped policy state: BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. Tail is elevated as delayed NQ holds near the premarket session low amid aligned yield and oil pressure.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES; current evidence shows elevated path risk until sustained retracement breaks the premarket downtrend.
headline: NQ holds near premarket low as yields and oil rise; Tail elevated
body: Delayed NQ was 29,213.25, down 1.02%, after trading from 29,571.25 to 29,184.25 and remaining near the low. Reuters reported Nasdaq-100 futures down 0.83% at 08:46 UTC, the U.S. 10-year yield near 4.79%, and Brent above $91 amid renewed U.S.-Iran/Hormuz risk.

sources.title: Wall St futures kick off September under pressure as yields, oil prices rise — Reuters
Bond selloff deepens and stocks drop as oil prices stoke inflation fears — Reuters

lookbackSummary: Across the prior 24 clock-hours, Tail stayed between 19% and 24%, moving from event/whipsaw into mixed conditions and never reaching elevated. Stress stayed 97-99%; the latest prior slot was WATCH at 24%.
outlookSummary: Current Tail is elevated at 31% because NQ is holding near a sharply lower premarket extreme with yields and oil aligned. Conditional Tail peaks at 38% around the 14:00 UTC data cluster only if the cash-open and releases extend the existing one-way structure; meaningful retracement would lower it.

forecast.analysis: Delayed NQ is 29,213.25, down 1.02% and only 29 points above the 29,184.25 session low after a 29,571.25 high. The observed premarket path is one-way enough to lift Tail into elevated territory, with 10Y yields near 4.79% and Brent above $91 reinforcing pressure.
drivers: NQ near session low after a roughly 387-point high-to-low swing

news.title: Wall St futures kick off September under pressure as yields, oil prices rise
Bond selloff deepens and stocks drop as oil prices stoke inflation fears

forecast.analysis: Tail remains conditionally elevated if NQ continues to hold near the premarket low or extends after weak rebounds. A sustained recovery away from the low would weaken the one-way-path evidence before the U.S. handoff.
Late-European trading keeps conditional Tail elevated if rebounds remain shallow and lower prices continue to gain acceptance. A broader retracement toward the overnight range would reduce path risk.

Barr's 13:05 UTC remarks and the approach to the cash open raise conditional path risk because the premarket trend is already weak. Tail stays elevated only if the existing downside structure persists rather than rotating two-sided.

The 14:00 UTC JOLTS, ISM Manufacturing and Construction Spending cluster is the peak conditional risk hour. High Tail assumes the existing downside structure survives the cash-open auction and the releases trigger further one-way repricing.
After the data cluster, Tail remains elevated only if the first impulse extends through failed or shallow retracements. An orderly two-sided response would move the path back toward WATCH.
A delayed second leg would keep Tail elevated if NQ remains near session extremes while yields and oil stay aligned. Visible mean reversion and volatility decay would materially reduce that risk.
Conditional Tail falls to WATCH if the afternoon develops broader two-sided rotation. Renewed extension from a weak rebound would keep the state near the elevated threshold.
WATCH assumes the market is beginning to digest the morning catalysts. Tail would rise again only if price re-establishes efficient directional movement with limited retracement.
Late-day Tail moderates if earlier extremes are retraced and cross-asset pressure stops intensifying. Persistent extreme holding would keep the path risk closer to the upper WATCH band.
In the U.S. cash-close hour, WATCH remains conditional on partial retracement. A fresh directional leg would require renewed confirmation from price structure rather than event importance alone.
In the first post-close hour, conditional Tail returns to low if the session has developed meaningful retracement. A close pinned near an extreme would invalidate that lower-risk path.
Early post-close conditions are expected to reduce directional pressure unless a geopolitical or rates shock creates a new catalyst. The forecast remains conditional on no fresh one-way extension.
Early Globex Tail is low if price discovery becomes more balanced after the U.S. session. Persistent oil or yield shocks could keep Stress extreme without automatically raising Tail.
Overnight risk stays low under a balanced futures path and absent new escalation. Stress remains extreme because the macro backdrop is still sensitive to rates and energy.
The overnight forecast remains low-Tail if mean reversion is visible and no new catalyst creates directional efficiency. Fresh geopolitical discontinuity would invalidate that baseline.
During the Asian handoff, low Tail assumes no renewed session-extreme holding. A clean directional break with shallow pullbacks would require reassessment.
Low Tail persists if Asian trading remains rotational and cross-assets stabilize. A new oil or yields impulse could raise Stress first, with Tail dependent on the NQ path response.
Toward Europe, conditional Tail edges higher because liquidity and macro sensitivity increase. The key test is whether the overnight range holds or gives way to efficient trend structure.
European opening conditions keep Tail near the low/watch boundary if price remains two-sided. A persistent break from the overnight range would raise the path-risk estimate.
WATCH becomes plausible if European flow reintroduces directional pressure, but the state remains conditional on actual extension rather than the macro backdrop alone.
Tail remains WATCH if Europe sustains a directional move with limited retracement. Stable yields and oil plus a balanced NQ path would pull it back toward low.
Late-Europe WATCH reflects the possibility that unresolved rates and energy pressure carries into the U.S. premarket. A balanced range would reduce Tail despite elevated Stress.
Ahead of the next U.S. premarket phase, WATCH reflects unresolved macro sensitivity. Tail would require fresh one-way NQ evidence to move above the threshold.

forecastDetail.comment: Observed NQ is near the session low after a sharp premarket decline; aligned yields and oil lift Tail into elevated territory.
Elevated Tail persists only if NQ keeps holding near the low or extends after weak rebounds; sustained recovery would lower it.
Late-Europe risk remains elevated if rebounds stay shallow and lower-price acceptance persists.
Barr and the cash-open approach matter because downside structure is already present; two-sided rotation would invalidate the elevated path.
Peak conditional risk: high Tail requires the cash-open/data sequence to extend the existing trend with weak retracement.
Post-data Tail stays elevated only on continued extension through failed or shallow pullbacks; orderly retracement would reduce it.
